How the interview runs

The Bloomberg SQL interview, as candidates report it

Bloomberg does not publish the format. Each row is what candidates and prep guides have described publicly, with its source; where sources disagree, the row says so. Formats change — treat every specific as reported, not official.

Data analyst stagesAn application, an online assessment (logic, English, Excel), a recruiter call, then a final round of three or four interviews that includes a 30–60 minute data exercise on a messy corporate-filings dataset.[1]
SQL screen for data rolesNot reliably reported. The assessment platform reported for Bloomberg is for software-engineering phone screens, not data roles, so this page names none. (no reliable source)
What the analyst round weighsReported as basic SQL and Excel alongside data-quality judgement — finding errors and proposing checks.[1]
  1. [1] OphyAI — Bloomberg interview guide (updated 3 Jun 2026)
  2. [2] DataLemur — Bloomberg SQL interview questions (17 Apr 2025)
  3. [3] DataLemur — stock min/max question (Bloomberg-tagged) (undated)

Sources: OphyAI — Bloomberg interview guide (updated 3 Jun 2026); DataLemur — Bloomberg SQL interview questions (17 Apr 2025); DataLemur — stock min/max question (Bloomberg-tagged) (undated). Accessed 13 Sep 2026.

The SQL that comes up

What Bloomberg SQL questions test

Reported most often, in order

  • 1Aggregation by time period (monthly and daily averages)
  • 2Joins, INNER vs LEFT
  • 3Window functions and ranking
  • 4Date-window filters
  • 5NULL handling
  • 6Second-highest value

Difficulty: Easy-to-medium. The data is daily prices, trades and volume, terminal sessions, exchange data subscriptions, and financial filings.

Our Bloomberg practice set, by skill

The 16 SQL Quest challenges tagged Bloomberg, resolved onto the nine Skillmap skills. A challenge exercises several skills, so shares do not sum to 100%. This is the composition of the practice set on this page, not a measurement of Bloomberg’s interview.

Sample questions

Bloomberg SQL question shapes, and where to practise them

Shapes candidates and guides report (paraphrased)

  • Daily stock prices by ticker: for each ticker, the month with the highest and the month with the lowest opening price.[3]
  • Trades by symbol and date: the average daily trading volume per symbol.[2]
  • Customers and exchange data subscriptions with start dates and status: US customers with an active subscription started in the last 30 days.[2]
